utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The artillery attacks were sporadic. They did not go on all the time. The fire would mount at moments, then there were periods of lull, and then fire would be renewed. It was altogether somewhat fiercer than during any other periods of time but nothing out of the ordinary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I just want to briefly look at the other report filed that day. That's P328. The original of this is very hard to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can you read it, Mr. Pandurevic? I'll hand you a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's blown up a little, I might be able to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'll hand you a hard copy. It's easier.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is the regular combat report of the 15th of July and this was sent at 11 minutes past 7.00 in the evening, about a quarter of an hour before the interim combat report, and under paragraph 1, it reads: "On the 15th of July, 1995, at around 4.40 in the morning, the enemy launched a heavy artillery attack on the defence lines of the 4th, 6th and 7th Battalions. The attack ended at about 5.30 but the enemy continued firing artillery and infantry weapons at short intervals?" Did you write that report or was that written by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report was drafted by the duty operations officer. It is obvious that we had the same or at least similar information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Which of those two reports more accurately reflects the situation on the ground on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The regular combat reports mention the names of the fallen soldiers; however, more detail about anything else that was happening on the ground is provided by the interim combat report. The intention of the interim combat report was certainly not to repeat the facts mentioned in the regular combat report, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Let's go to the third paragraph. If we can have P329 put back on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: "Enemy attacks were vigorously supported by all calibres of artillery and tanks. Attacks of varying intensity followed one another from the direction of Nezuk and Kalesija on Memici. The attack on Memici is still in progress. All targets deep inside the territory and the suburbs and town of Zvornik have been under artillery fire. All attacks have been repulsed successfully so far. So far, according to information received, we have four dead and a dozen or so wounded. With all available forces, we have sealed off the wider area of Crni Vrh and Planici and partially the area of Kamenica. All brigade forces are fully engaged and we have no reserves." Where did the information in that paragraph come from?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information in that paragraph, particularly the part that refers to the past time, is something that I received on the ground, and the information about the current situation is something that I personally witnessed. When this report was drafted, there was no artillery fire opened on the IKM sector or the city of Zvornik opened. All the artillery fire had been opened earlier in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: How accurately did that paragraph reflect the military situation at about 7.00 in the evening, when you were dictating the report to -- sorry, I shouldn't say that. How accurately did that paragraph in the report reflect the military situation when you were dictating the report to Ljubo Bojanovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that information that I received about the events that had happened before I arrived is correct and that this passage reflects that situation. I also believe that what I had noted about the blockade of the Crni Vrh, Planici and Kamenica, it was also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 4. "An additional burden for us is the large number of prisoners distributed throughout schools in the brigade area, as well as obligations of security and restoration of the terrain." Were you aware of any order or instruction not to mention prisoners in any oral or written communication at that time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to the moment when Mr. Grujic conveyed the information to me about the existence of POWs, I did not have any information about them or the fact that there was a ban on reporting their existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So did you think there was anything wrong in writing this report and explicitly referring to the prisoners you'd heard about?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believed that this should be conveyed to the corps command. At that moment I did not have any reliable information as to where they had come from, why they were there, and I fully believed that the corps command would react upon the receipt of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Why the corps command?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that was my superior command who were the recipients of my reports in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What did you mean when you said the prisoners were a burden to the brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole report mentions certain facts and information of different significance. The term "additional burden" does not mean the same as if we had been given a task or were under some obligation towards the prisoners; however, this just shows that those people were there and might present a burden in different ways. For example, there could be reactions of the families of the fighters who resided close to the locations where POWs were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, did you intend the references to what in Serbian is "asanacija" and what has been translated as "security of the terrain" to refer to guarding and burying prisoners in the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, leading. "What did you intend that to mean?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, can you rephrase it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't think that's a leading question. He is entitled to answer the case that's put against him absolutely. That's the Prosecution case. He is entitled to answer that as steadfastly as he is entitled to enter a not-guilty plea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I absolutely agree, but he first needs to set the foundation by letting the witness say what he intends. That's the important thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I've got nothing further to say. I'd like you to rule on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Our conclusion is that we consider the question as put as leading, to be a leading one, and we therefore suggest that you rephrase it and possibly agree to the way suggested by Mr. McCloskey. Of course, you will be able to follow it through once you have rephrased the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, when you wrote this report, what did you believe to be the state of health of the prisoners that Brano Grujic had referred to?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about the state of the prisoners. I just stated in the report that they were present and that was all, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you know whether anybody had been executed?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you know whether anybody had been buried?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you know about any plan to execute or bury prisoners?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In this paragraph, when you referred to "obligations of security and restoration of the terrain," as we have it in English, what were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was dictating this report, I knew what I was referring to, I knew what I meant to say. I used the appropriate words to convey that. "Obligations of security," that is the wrong translation. These words mean support. "Asanacija" is a military term and it's well known what it means and what it refers to, and that's the way I used it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Let's deal with "asanacija" first. As a military term, what responsibilities did you regard that as placing upon the brigade at the time you wrote the report?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military commanders have the duty to carry out "asanacija" of the battle-field or of the terrain on which combat is carried out. That's what I meant. "Asanacija" involves a number of activities and stages. One of the first activities or stages in "asanacija" is finding and taking care of the wounded and sending them to appropriate facilities, then finding the corpses of those who had been killed. After combat, complete "asanacija" has to be carried out, which means inspecting the terrain and removing any remains that would be a threat to the lives of people or that might cause epidemics on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What work did you anticipate would need to be done by brigade resources in the event of a fully contested battle involving your forces, the forces of the 2nd Corps and the forces of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fighting was already going on. There was combat starting early in the morning of the 15th, as we have already said. There was sporadic fighting on the left flank in the course of the day. Those three men in the medical corps had already been killed, in the medical vehicle, so that was already something that involved the first stage of "asanacija". If you have a single wounded man, you need at least two or three soldiers who are fit to take him to the field hospital and therefore you have fewer men to be used in fighting, so this is certainly a burden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder if we could just have a quick look at another document while we're considering this one, and it's 7D480, please. We're going to need page 6 in the English -- I'm sorry, page 6 in the B/C/S, page 5 in the English. This is "The Federal Secretariat for National Defence Instructions on Hygiene and Sanitation Measures in Battle-fields of 1991."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, can you see the whole of point 2 there, which is what I wanted to refer you to?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, now I can see all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It reads that: "Hygienic and sanitation measures in battle-fields include the following: Finding the wounded who are accidentally left behind, gathering them, giving them first aid and evacuating them to medical institutions; finding, gathering and helping wounded or diseased animals and animals that were accidentally left behind; finding, gathering and burying or burning those who have been killed or have died of natural causes and establishing the necessary records; finding, gathering and removing animal carcasses ..." and so on and so forth. Does that conform with your understanding of what hygienic and sanitation measures on a battle-field were required of you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. At the military academy, we had a special subject, rear support, and "asanacija" of the battle-ground was dealt with in that subject. So this is all familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we go back to P329, please, and can we go to the second page in the B/C/S only.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I don't know if a pen can be made available to you, General Pandurevic. I wonder if you could just mark for us, please, the last four words of the second paragraph on that page.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want you to give us a word in Serbian now, please. If you were referring to your security organ or security service, what word would you use?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would use the word security -- "bezbednosno" or "obezbedjenje," security support.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, what word would you use to say "security organ"?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Organ bezbednosti."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Chief of security?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Nacelnik bezbednosti."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Would you read the last four words of that paragraph, please. And I don't want them translated.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Obaveze obezbedjenja i asanacije terena."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I want another document put onto the screen, please. Can we have P6 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to save this one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Would you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sign and put the date, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: -- initial that.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And it's time for the break --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- any time you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It would be a good time now, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's make sure that the witness signs ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My signature is already there, but I can put another one on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We'll have a 25-minute break.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder if we could just illustrate this point graphically by placing into e-court, please, P407.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: These are the rules of service of the security organs, and in Serbian, "security organs" appears as "organa bezbednosti"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, "organa bezbednosti," that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, the words which you circled for us on P329 include the word "obezbedjenja." I wonder if, so that we've got it clear on the screen, you would just spell that word for us, because you wrote it in Cyrillic or, rather, Ljubo Bojanovic wrote it in Cyrillic. So would you spell that word in Latin letters.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. O-b-e-z-b-e-d, with a diacritic or alternatively "dj," e-n-j-a.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And so that we're clear, can you see that word on the document we have on the screen now, the rules of service of security organs?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, we can't see that word on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we have now, please, into e-court P694, the brigade rules, chapter 5.3; the B/C/S page 105, the English page 65.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, do we see on that document the word "obezbedjenja" that you put in your report as the heading to chapter 3?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see here under number 3, "bezbednosti" or "obezbedjenje," but that's something different from "obezbedjenje" of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do we also see the word there used for security in terms of the security organs, "organa bezbednosti"? So we've got both of the words we've been talking about juxtaposed on this document; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we have a look, please, at the same document, page 56 in the English, page 92 in the B/C/S. And this is P694, just for the correction of the transcript at line 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Again, simple question, Mr. Pandurevic: At the heading of chapter 5, do we see again the word "obezbedjenja" that you wrote in that report?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what, just so that we're clear, are "borbenih dejstava"?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Borbenih dejstava" is an overall term covering all kinds of combat activities in fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we have a look now, please, at P699, and we want page 93 in the English and page 100 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Again, in the heading of chapter 5, do we see the word you used in the report, P329, again "obezbedjenja"?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we know now what the last two words you understand to be, so we can move on from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we have a look at the same document, please, page 116 in the English, page 125 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again, at the heading of chapter 10, in that document, do we see the word you used in your report, P329, "obezbedjenja"?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we see the same word here, "obezbedjenja."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, at the time of writing the interim combat report of the 15th of July, were you aware of any measures that had been taken to cope with the problem of "obezbedjenja terena" within the brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In part some measures had been taken, but most of the measures still had to be taken as concerns the roads and the rear of the forces of the Zvornik Brigade. This activity followed later on the 15th and in the morning of the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It probably wasn't a very good question, but what men were going to be used to deal with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection; vague. Deal with what? We haven't established what this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think Mr. McCloskey is right, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What's the R Battalion?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise. Let me just say this word, "obezbedjenja" of the terrain, is a combat activity carried out by units. The R Battalion is the reserve battalion which was mobilised when required by combat conditions, was supposed to carry out the tasks of "obezbedjenja" of the terrain, the general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Let's have a look, please, at a few documents, therefore. Can we start with P377, the duty officer's notebook. You will need to look at page 756, and the rest of us at page 138.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm interested in the entry about Mr. Galic. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Galic was the assistant of the Chief of Staff for organisation, mobilisation, and personnel in the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And when it says, "Galic to mobilise all able-bodied men," as simply as you can, what would that have involved him doing?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was supposed to send a request through the corps command to the department of the Ministry of Defence to mobilise the R Battalion, and above Galic's name we see the name of Jagodic and the telephone number. That's the person who was doing that job in the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the Ministry of Defence, shall we? 7D775, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is a document signed by Stevan Ivanovic. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevan Ivanovic was the chief of the department of the Ministry of Defence in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And it's dated the 15th of July, it's from the Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence Zvornik Secretariat, and it says: "For the purposes of guarding the territory in the zone of responsibility from infiltrated sabotage groups and broken-up Muslim groups from Srebrenica, immediately mobilise on all conscripts fit for military service from the area of the Zvornik municipality department who have not been assigned to RJ's war units." And if we go to the first line there, what do the third and fourth words say in Serbian, Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The words used were "obezbedjenja teritorije."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What is the difference between "teritorije" and "terena"?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are synonyms; they mean the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now can we go to 7D109.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you just help us as to what that document is?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a document issued by the Ministry of Defence and it shows the procedure followed when carrying out mobilisation of conscripts in this case. It shows that the instruction issued by the Ministry of Defence was complied with in the process of mobilisation, and the secretariat in Zvornik is called upon at the request of the Drina Corps. So the command of the Zvornik Brigade could not do this directly; it had to go through the corps command. And this shows that the procedure was complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. Can we now look at 7D109 so we can follow the process through.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Another document from Stevan Ivanovic in which he orders: "In order to secure the territory in the corps' zone of responsibility, immediately complete mobilisation of all conscripts fit for military duty from the territory ..." et cetera. And the phrase in the top line of that order is what?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Obezbedjenja."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we have 1D698, please, a Drina Corps order of the 5th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes, just to be clear in the transcripts, I think twice we're getting a reference to 1D709, and that might cause us problems later, at 11 and 12 on page 55, and then again at line 4 on page 56.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Judge Prost. The document I called into e-court is 7D709, and I do not have 1D709 on my list of documents for examination of this witness. I do have 1D698, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: 1D698, what is this document, Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was issued by the corps command. In it the corps addresses the Ministry of Defence with the request for urgent mobilisation of conscripts with a view to securing the territory in the zone of responsibility of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do we see that word "obezbedjenja" appearing there as well?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the first line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, to complete the picture, can we have a look, please, at 3D125. The English translation is only partial because it's a list of names, so it doesn't really matter. But there is one correction that needs to be made to the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What's this document, Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was issued by the Zvornik section of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what does it record?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Zvornik section of the Ministry of Defence informs the Zvornik Brigade, i.e., military post 7149 Zvornik, which conscripts had been called on 15th July and who was supposed to be mobilised. This was for the Zvornik Brigade in order to be able to collate their lists with this one and see whether all the conscripts who had been mobilised reported to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And you've probably already confirmed this, but on the English version it suggests that the date of mobilisation was the 17th of July. What's the date of mobilisation on the original?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The report was drafted on the 17th and the conscripts were called on the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: How many of them were called? You might need to go to the last page of the document to see that.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last digits are 254 [as interpreted], as far as I can see, but I believe that the last digit is not correct. That was the number called, but it doesn't have to mean that everybody responded.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, we'll come on to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we have a look, please, at P377, page 768 for you, and for the rest of us, 150.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: About a third to half the way down the page, can you see a reference to the R Battalion?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, R Battalion is mentioned. It says that 195 were mobilised and are ready in Standard at 1740 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It might seem obvious, Mr. Pandurevic, but you have to give the evidence, not me. What does that tell us when we compare it to a list of 245 men who were mobilised by order by the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They called 245; however, only 195 responded and reported at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just remind us, what were those men mobilised to do?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Obezbedjenja terena," or territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we get a definition of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Oh, we're coming on to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: From the booth?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I know the booth is trying to be cooperative and I think that's good, but I think I have a right to know what that means in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have been -- yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just as I sit here, I recall that sometimes it's very difficult for the booth to tell what something means because of the context it's in. If that's the situation here, we can just leave it and we'll try to sort it out ourselves, as opposed to them guessing or going along with the context they're not clear about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not how I have understood things to be developing, but Mr. Haynes, perhaps, can clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What I was going to move on to do next was ask Mr. Pandurevic to specify what tasks these men were to be put to, which will give us a better understanding of what the phrase meant in the document, according to him. We have already the word, I think, "obezbedjenja" translated in four different ways in the documents we have before us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop. We can proceed, because that more or less -- not more or less. It actually tallies with how we were viewing your approach.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's proceed, and then if you are not happy, Mr. McCloskey, you will make submissions to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's no problem. I don't need to put the booth in that spot. We'll sort it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, given the situation on the ground on the 15th of July, what did you need to mobilise these 200 men, give or take a handful, to actually do?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order for us to understand the situation better, I'll try and provide a short explanation of the situation on the ground on the 15th. We know that most of the column of the 28th Division crossed the Crni Vrh-Zvornik road. We also know that elements of the 28th Division remained in the territories of Snagovo and Kamenica as well. We also knew at the time that the Zvornik-Crni Vrh road was not safe. In order to provide security or support for our forces which were blocking the better part of the 28th Division, we had to mobilise additional forces to secure the terrain. That's why we mobilised this R Battalion. As for their task of providing security, or "obezbedjenja," for the terrain, it was carried out by way of setting up ambushes, blockades, carrying out patrols, and setting up observation points. These were all types of combat actions which are comprised in the overall task of providing security or securing the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Let's have a look at how in fact they were used. Can we have a look at P377, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, you will need to turn to page 772; the rest of us, to page 154. And we see at the top of that page: "R Battalion to join men from Bratunac to be given one combat set of ammunition and take up the Crni Vrh-Planici line. It should leave at 7.00 a.m. The line was taken up at 8.00 a.m. The commander to call Petrovic regarding communications. Distribute 1.800." Tell us a little bit about what that means.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a task given to R Battalion once the R Battalion was mobilised and brought up to strength. This shows that they were sent to Crni Vrh where they were to join the Bratunac men who had already been on the -- securing the terrain detail. Pursuant to my report or based on my interim combat report drafted on the 15th, General Krstic also sent some of the Vlasenica military brigade elements to carry out the same task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we now just follow that through by looking at page 775 in the original book, or page 157 for the rest of us. Here we see it says at the bottom of the page: "The R Battalion took up positions between quarry in Grbavci and Crni Vrh, 163 conscripts and 80 conscripts from Bratunac. The platoon deployed on the Devanje-Kruska [phoen] line returned from that position." There were 195 at Standard earlier that day. Do you know what the other 32 were doing?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who were supposed to report to Standard, I believe that that number is correct. However, I believe that some of those men were also demobilised, because brigade commanders would know some people and would demobilise them, and I believe that the rest remained in the barracks, in the rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we go back to P329 now. You will need to see page 2. Indeed, everybody who speaks your language will need to see page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: When, in paragraph 4 of that report, you referred to "obezbedjenja terena," what obligation of the brigade were you reporting to corps command?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That is not what he says in the document. I don't mind a reading of the document, but that's counsel's interpretation. I could read it in B/C/S and that's not what it would say, literally. So I think he can just say what he means by that last sentence, but please don't misquote it like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't think it requires a contribution, Your Honour. I'm sure the witness can answer the question however I phrased it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, you followed the exchange of comments and you can go straight to the point, please, particularly explaining to us what you mean by "obezbedjenja terena" and "asanacija".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that this document is one that has been quoted most and interpreted most of all that I've ever written, and I believe that it has been misinterpreted and things have been taken out of the context quite a lot. What I'm saying is that this report is one whole, and that in the first part of this report, on the first page thereof, I speak about every single problem that the brigade encountered at the time and which arose from the combat situation. And at the end I state in this document that all the brigade forces were fully engaged, that I had no more reserve forces at my disposal. And I also say that there is an additional burden as a special problem and also I add this obligation of "obezbedjenja" and "asanacija" and I -- what I mean is combat activities undertaken by the units of the Bratunac Brigade and the R Battalion. In other words, this obligation of "obezbedjenja" and "asanacija" were -- are current obligations and also obligations which continued throughout the next few following days.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you referring in that report to guarding and burying prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This passage may be interpreted from the linguistic point of view but it would take other kinds of experts to do that. I can only interpret it from the aspect of the essence of the matter that is contained here. This has nothing to do with guarding prisoners or burying their bodies. It cannot even be suggested by the words that were used in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we move on to paragraph 5 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This command cannot take care of these problems any longer, as it has neither the material nor the resources. If no one takes on this responsibility, I will be forced to let them go: "I made an offer to the commander of the other side to separate out the civilians and have the other surrender, but he refused asking that they should all be released together. The situation is still complicated but under control." What did you mean in that section referring to "these problems" and "this responsibility"?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since General Krstic ordered me to go back to Zvornik and gave me concrete tasks, and that concrete task was to prevent a break through of the 28th Division and its linking up with the forces of the 2nd Corps, I explained my problem to him. I told him about the situation, about the forces that I had available to me in the brigade, and in this paragraph here, I indicated that I would let them go because that's the decision that I had reached after my conversations with Mr. Semso Muminovic. And when I say that I would let them go is confirmed in the next sentence which reads, "I offer the commander on the opposite side that the civilians should be separated and that the rest would surrender," which was turned down, and we were asked to let everybody go. I am talking about the column of the 28th Division and of them being let go. Later on, this was confirmed by the events on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that on the 16th, the column was let go, they were get through.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: At the time of writing this report, did you have any idea how many prisoners were in the schools in the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have a figure in mind. I didn't know that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: How many schools were being used?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I remember Grujic having mentioned school in Petkovci and Pilica. I didn't know anything about which schools existed in the territory of the municipality, whether POWs were housed in all of the schools or not, I didn't know that at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What was your purpose in writing this report in these terms to corps command on the evening of the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My purpose was to inform the corps command and let them gain a complete insight into the situation in the territory of Zvornik or rather in the zone of responsibility and defence of the Zvornik Brigade, especially bearing in mind the task which brought me back from the territory of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Why did you threaten in that document to let the column of the 28th Division go?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already told you, the tone of my entire report was set so as to enable me to say at the end that I would be forced to let the column go especially after the conversation that I had had with Semso Muminovic. All who had Motorolas at the time could listen to our conversations, and in some way, I wanted to use the report indirectly to let the corps command know what my final decision would be when it came to the column of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more thing on that day. Given what you'd been told earlier by Brano Grujic, why did you not try and find out as much as possible about the prisoners he told you about?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I'm talking about these events, and as I'm reading the documents and especially this report, I'm trying to place myself in the past. I'm trying to go back in time and put myself in the role that I played at the time because that's the only way one can understand the events; and I would ask the same question if I'd been anybody else but the commander at the time. First of all, General Krstic had sent me back with a clear task. He did not give me any alternative information or information of any other kind. All he gave me was a combat task. Second of all, the information that I was provided about the prisoners, I did try to check that information with Ljubo Bojanovic who was in a position to know something more if the command of the Zvornik Brigade had been issued with such a task. Since I did not receive any additional information, any information pointing to the fact that the command of the Zvornik Brigade was supposed to deal with POWs, and I also did not receive any information to the effect that those people were treated in any way that was against the law; and I also sent a report to the corps in which I mentioned POWs, and I expected that if the corps did not know anything about this, they would ask for some additional information or they would order me as to what to do. However, I never received any feedback from the corps with this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where did you spend the night on the 15th and 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the forward command post in the prefabricated building there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you remain there throughout the day of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what was the focus of your attention throughout the night of the 15th and 16th?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this period of the information I had, I drew up the task that we read out here addressed to all the battalions, in readiness to have them all go at 4.00 a.m. in -- with weapons in their hands and boots on their feet ready to meet an enemy attack. I was awake at that time at the observation post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did that attack materialise?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early morning hours, there was an attack by the 2nd Corps. It was focused on the positions of the 4th and 7th Battalions and partly the positions of the 6th. And they had artillery support.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm going to leave that there until tomorrow and as it were look at some parallel events now. Can we have a look at P377. You will need to look at page 761 and we'll have to look at page 143. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, firstly can you help us by perhaps looking back in the book to ascertain what time on what date the entries at the top of that page would have been made, approximately?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sentence that begins with the word, "Early in the morning to report to Major Golic," is that what you are referring to, Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic would report to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you whether you can place a time on that entry.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it says in the morning, probably on the following day, and that's the 15th in the afternoon or evening, as it says in this notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Who is Major Golic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew a certain Major Pavle Golic who worked in the intelligence organ of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we go forward two pages please to page 763 in the original which you have and pages 145 in the document we have. And here, the entry I'm interested in, we can place a time on, 8.45. Again, here we see Golic asked Popovic to call them and said that he can forget what he asked for and what he wrote about. He knows what he's supposed to do according to agreed procedure, "Boss from panorama, message conveyed to Popovic at 9.10." Who is the boss from Panorama?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Panorama was the code-name for the Main Staff and when it's used next to 01, that refers to the commander of the Main Staff. Just as I was Palma 01.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If we go to the entry at the bottom of the page, there's a reference to Panorama 155, does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say code-name or when you use a code-name, whether it's Palma, Panorama, or Zlatar, and a three-digit number next to it, you are referring to an extension. So this is an extension in the Main Staff from that number that the code refers to. I don't know whose it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we go over the page, please, to page 764 in the original book and page 146 in the e-court document. At 11.15 there is an entry relating to a report from Zlatar. You've already told us what Zlatar was, but can you remind us?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody from the command of the Drina Corps is telling the duty officer of the Zvornik Brigade conveying the message that screening of the wounded has to be carried out and it says here in brackets that this was conveyed to Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you know he was at the command of the Zvornik Brigade on the morning of the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we go forward to page 766 in the original, please, and page 148 in the e-court version of this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: 1400 hours, "Popovic requested a bus with a full tank and 500 litres of D2. Zlatar duty officer and Golic informed." Did you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you approve anybody being given a bus or any fuel on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And at 2.00 in the afternoon of the 16th of July, did you know that anybody called Popovic was at the command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We'll come on to it in a bit more detail. What were you doing at 2.00 in the afternoon on the 16th of July and where were you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 2.00 p.m. on the 16th of July, I was close to the corridor we had opened up and overseeing the passage of the column of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we just have a quick look please at P1189 A in the English and C in the B/C/S. It's under seal in the Serbian but not in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you know who Basevic is?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Major Tomislav Basevic who was the chief of the technical service in the rear of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: When a duty officer says over the radio, "Somebody is in the field." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the original before me. Could it please be shown to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Certainly, it's a two-page document, and it's probably easier for you to look at the hard copy. We may all appreciate going to page 2 for a little while.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please repeat your question now?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. If a duty officer says that a certain person is in the field, what does that tell us about their location?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we have a misconnect here. We're getting a hypothetical question and the witness thinks he's referring specifically to the document and if -- I think we should do one or the other but not both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: To say that I'm astonished to receiving the objection from that quarter, that would be putting it mildly, but I will correct the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page in English, the Palma duty officer is recorded as saying, "Well I don't know. He just called me from the field and told me to pass you the message over there." That person is said to be the Palma duty officer. If a duty officer says that somebody has called from the field, what does that tend to mean about their whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that the person who called the duty officer of Palma was somewhere out on the ground, not at the command from where they can use communications to achieve contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll leave it there for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes. We will continue tomorrow in the afternoon at 2.15, correct? Thank you. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic. All right. Okay. Thank you. So we stand adjourned to tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.45, to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd day of February, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.
